# HELMET

> HELMET is a small PHP package that sends the security headers and a nonce-based CSP, hardens the session, checks the proxy, answers /up and writes JSON logs. Raw PHP, Laravel and PSR-15 apps all use the same core.

GIF via [Tenor](https://tenor.com/view/helmet-band-wilmas-rainbow-helmet-band-music-gif-25658120)

**Put it on before you ship.** Security headers, a hardened session and an honest proxy check, snapped on before
the first page is served.

Checks: `composer ci` (the same command runs on GitLab and GitHub).
Two mirrors, one command: the only thing in this repo that plays both sides is the CI.
Front page: [`site/index.html`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/site/index.html), the playbook, as static files ([`site/README.md`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/site/README.md)).
On Citadel it is served by the raw-PHP deploy layer in [`deploy/`](https://github.com/waynestate/helmet/blob/HEAD/deploy/): a Squire kit whose front controller serves `site/` behind HELMET's security headers. For local development, keep serving `site/` directly.

HELMET is the Wayne State app stack's baseline runtime. One small
framework-free PHP core, `Waynestate\Helmet`, does the five things every app on
Citadel needs before it serves a single page: it sends the security headers,
hardens the session, decides whether the request really arrived over HTTPS,
answers the load balancer's `/up` ping, and writes structured logs.

This repository is published from Wayne State University's internal
GitLab and mirrored here. Changes land there first; Wayne State
developers open issues and merge requests on the internal project.

It is the floor, not the ceiling. An app on raw PHP calls `helmet_boot()` once
at the top of its front controller and is done. An app on Laravel or a PSR-15
stack mounts the same core as middleware and gets the identical headers. The
rules live in one place, and every consumer path agrees.

Every page below is Markdown. The HTML pages send the same Markdown to a client that asks for `text/markdown`. Written by Squire's agent-ready kit from the README and the pages; do not edit.

## Pages

- [HELMET: Put it on before you ship.](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md): HELMET is a small PHP package that sends the security headers and a nonce-based CSP, hardens the session, checks the proxy, answers /up and writes JSON logs. Raw PHP, Laravel and PSR-15 apps all use the same core.

## Prompts

- [Get started with HELMET](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-get-started): The agent works out your app's shape and where it runs, then writes the smallest plan to add HELMET. It changes nothing yet. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a raw PHP app](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-raw-php): Adds helmet_boot() to the front controller and the nonce to each inline script. If some pages skip the front controller, it adds public/up.php too. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a Laravel app with Blade](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-blade): Publishes the config, sets the platform and puts the nonce on inline scripts in Blade. Laravel keeps its own /up and its own session settings. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a Laravel app with Inertia and Vue](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-laravel-inertia): The Laravel setup, then a search for what the CSP will break: scripts in Inertia's Head, a second package that makes nonces, and HTML cached across requests. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
- [HELMET in a PSR-15 middleware pipeline](https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/#prompt-psr15): Adds HealthCheck and SecurityHeadersMiddleware to your pipeline. Your handlers read the nonce from the helmet.csp_nonce attribute. The prompt itself is in https://helmet.apps.wayne.edu/index.md.
